clue.text: US civilians, perhaps, going west to register

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading the letters right to left

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers, so civilians might be non-GIs

explanation.surface: American civilians heading west to sign up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading NONGIS backwards gives the answer. GI is a US enlisted soldier, so US civilians are NON-GIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign on is to enrol or register, for a job or for benefits.

definitions.meaning: long side whiskers grown down the cheeks

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dining-room cabinet and British slang for long sideburns.

definitions.meaning: rank as an adjective means flagrant or coarse

explanation.definitionFit: The word means rank or flagrant, and also twelve dozen, 144.

clue.text: Effective production on stage not shortened

parts.note: an opera is a staged musical production
n't is the contracted, shortened form of not

explanation.surface: A stage show that runs at full length and works well.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the contraction n't, as in 'can't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means producing an effect, working, so effective.

parts.note: someone who mixed at a party was being sociable

indicators.note: about tells you to turn the next word round

parts.note: gab means idle talk or chatter

explanation.surface: A question about whether chatting at a party counts as a medley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the turnaround signal on talk; 'Was sociable' reads as one person mingling, not a word for mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-pourri is an assorted mixture, which is just what a mixed bag is.

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: off tells you the letters go wrong and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry to begin, while someone gets ripped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal on torn; the 's of one's is just 'is', giving no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the start of a piece of music or a talk.

clue.text: European politician has links with dead men

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: A politician from the continent with connections to the deceased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead men' is British slang for empty bottles after a party, not corpses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead men is slang for drained bottles, which are also called empties.

clue.text: People used to high living wound us beneath

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted round, says the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Mountain people injuring someone lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind, the anagram signal for US BENEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bhutanese live in the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan, at high altitude.

clue.text: Look amazed when beast appears after midnight

indicators.note: appears after puts the beast behind that letter

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night
an ape is a beast

explanation.surface: Staring in shock as a creature turns up in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as mid-night, the centre letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to stare open-mouthed in wonder.

clue.text: It's drunk and it's eaten in mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink, also a food in the army canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like a military dining hall but signals rearranging IT'S EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is an aniseed-flavoured liqueur, something you drink.

clue.text: Literary family and teachers go ballistic

parts.note: the Doones are the outlaw clan in R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A family from a novel, and some schoolteachers, who lose their tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doones are the outlaw family in Lorna Doone. The NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for losing your temper completely, British slang where 'nut' means the head.

definitions.meaning: to ... for something is to choose it

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a verb meaning to choose firmly and an adjective meaning chubby.

clue.text: Break with continuity, sorting Hudson Bay mails

indicators.note: sorting the letters puts them into a new order, as a post office sorts mail

explanation.surface: Post being sorted from Canada, with the clerk taking a break that feels just like work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting' rearranges the letters of HUDSON BAY MAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A busman's holiday is a break spent doing much the same as your daily job, so work carries on unbroken.

parts.note: a buddy is a pal or sidekick

indicators.note: ignoring lead means dropping the first letter

parts.note: wholly means completely

explanation.surface: A partner who pays no attention to the frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring lead' takes the W off WHOLLY to give HOLLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddy Holly was an American rock and roll singer of the 1950s.

clue.text: Humble abode for poet when starting course

indicators.note: starting says this piece comes at the front

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
cot is an old poetic word for a small cottage

explanation.surface: A poet's little cottage at the start of some venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' puts the word for when at the front. Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, famous for Royal Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English horse-racing course, so it is an example of a course.

definitions.meaning: a request to repeat yourself, like pardon
to come back to a place

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial way of saying pardon, and literally means to return.

clue.text: Philosopher after Diderot's ultimate collection for union

indicators.note: after puts the philosopher behind that single letter
ultimate means the final letter of the word next to it

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an eighteenth-century French philosopher

explanation.surface: One French thinker following another's last work, a compilation.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of Diderot, T, goes before ROUSSEAU. Diderot and Rousseau were contemporaries, which helps the misleading surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage, a union.

parts.note: over means left over, surplus
to haul is to carry or transport

explanation.surface: Repairing extra lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to examine and repair it thoroughly.

clue.text: Syrian mother with a part in a play

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a scene is one section of a play

explanation.surface: A Syrian mother who gets a role in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene means from Damascus, the capital of Syria.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Winning a few trophies at the London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club; 'Bag' looks like a verb meaning win.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, often for school books.

clue.text: Bloomers, say, reproduced for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means said out loud, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: animals that bred have reproduced

explanation.surface: Ladies' underwear being copied for spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like old-fashioned knickers, but a bloomer is a British crusty loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a kind of loaf, so bloomers are an example of the staple food.

clue.text: A scribe working somewhere in Lombardy

indicators.note: working means put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A copyist busy in northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges A SCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in the Lombardy region of northern Italy.

definitions.meaning: the finest, most worthy people are called this idiom
halite is rock salt, literally salt dug from the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the best of people, and taken literally describes rock salt, mined from the ground.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Drugs found after reading something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' is slang for information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal slang for information, the facts.

indicators.note: vocal says the word is spoken, so it sounds like the answer

parts.note: Ray's, belonging to a man called Ray

explanation.surface: A man's spoken word standing upright.
explanation.walkthrough: RAY'S, of a man named Ray, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to erect it or put it up.

indicators.note: mount means climb, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A mountain ahead of another mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'mount' means rise, reversing ANTE in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily, so a mount.

definitions.meaning: the pirate Blackbeard's real name was Edward ...
to train someone is to instruct them

explanation.definitionFit: The pirate Blackbeard was Edward Teach, and the same word means to instruct or train.

clue.text: Lord's house in a bad way in Marlborough

parts.note: a church is the house of the Lord
ill means unwell, in a bad way

explanation.surface: A nobleman's stately home falling into disrepair in a Wiltshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlborough is not the town: Churchill is the family name of the Dukes of Marlborough. 'Lord' looks like a peer but is God.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dukes of Marlborough carry the family surname Churchill, Winston being of that line.

indicators.note: heard tells you the word is taken as spoken, not as written

parts.note: an analyst works in a laboratory testing samples

explanation.surface: A scientist overheard by someone keeping notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, yearly chronicles, so is a recorder of events.

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the tree

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Something only just left hanging in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Just about' reads as one phrase, but only 'Just' defines; 'about' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means only just, by the narrowest margin.
